name: Merck
description: Merck (MSD outside the US and Canada) discovers, makes and sells prescription medicines, vaccines and animal-health products. Pharmaceutical sales were 89 percent of 2025 revenue and Animal Health 10 percent. Money comes from selling patent-protected drugs, mostly through wholesalers and pharmacy and hospital channels, at prices negotiated with insurers and governments. One product carries the company: Keytruda, a cancer immunotherapy given by infusion, was 49 percent of total 2025 sales, and its main compound patent expires in December 2028 in the US. The pharmaceutical segment earns about a 79 percent segment margin before research spending, which Merck does not allocate to segments. In 2026 Merck spent heavily on acquisitions (Cidara $9.2B in January, Terns $6.8B in May), which pushed reported pre-tax income negative in Q2 and the first half of 2026.

gics.note: Industry group and industry are not shown in the source read, so they are null. SEC SIC code 2834 (Pharmaceutical Preparations), from the EDGAR submissions record.

hq.note: 126 East Lincoln Avenue, Rahway, NJ 07065 (SEC EDGAR business address). The Wikipedia S&P 500 table still lists Kenilworth, NJ.

employees.note: Approximately 75,000 employees worldwide (about 30,000 in the US incl. Puerto Rico), plus about 15,000 third-party contractors; FY2025 10-K

businessLines.name: Pharmaceutical
businessLines.shareBasis: Share of revenue = 58,142 / 65,011 total. Share of profit = 45,754 / (45,754 + 2,131) segment profits only.
businessLines.how: Merck sells to wholesalers and retailers, hospitals, government agencies and managed-care organizations including pharmacy benefit managers (10-K), at prices net of chargebacks, discounts and rebates; revenue is per dose or per course while patents last. Alliance products (Lynparza, Lenvima, Reblozyl, Adempas/Verquvo outside Merck's territories) book only Merck's profit share or royalty, not the partner's sales.
businessLines.description: Human-health prescription drugs and vaccines: oncology (Keytruda, Keytruda Qlex, Welireg, Lynparza and Lenvima alliance revenue), vaccines (Gardasil, ProQuad/M-M-R II/Varivax, Capvaxive, Vaxneuvance, RotaTeq), cardiometabolic and respiratory (Winrevair, Ohtuvayre, Adempas), infectious disease (Bridion, Prevymis) and diabetes (Januvia, Janumet).

operatingProfit.note: Segment profit = segment sales less standard costs and directly incurred SG&A. It excludes most cost of sales, all Merck Research Laboratories R&D, amortization and restructuring, so it is not comparable with an operating income.

businessLines.name: Animal Health
businessLines.how: Products are sold per unit to customers in two lines, livestock and companion animals; the 10-K describes Bravecto doses lasting from one month to up to one year, i.e. repeat purchases per pet. Channel detail (veterinarians, distributors) was not extracted.
businessLines.description: Animal-health products sold into two lines, Livestock and Companion Animal; the companion line includes Bravecto, a range of oral, topical and injectable parasite-control products for dogs and cats (10-K).

revenue.note: FY2024 $5,877M; H1 2026 $3,566M vs $3,234M. Livestock $3,896M and Companion Animal $2,458M in FY2025.

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $5,877M; H1 2026 $3,566M vs $3,234M. Livestock $3,896M and Companion Animal $2,458M in FY2025.

operatingProfit.note: Segment profit; here it is after all cost of sales, SG&A and R&D directly incurred by the segment (a fuller cost load than the Pharmaceutical segment profit)

brands.name: Bravecto
brands.note: Named in the 10-K as a key product; its revenue was not extracted

brands.name: MSD
brands.note: Merck uses the MSD name outside the US and Canada

whatsNext.text: Bridion loses US market exclusivity in July 2026; Merck expects to discontinue US sales by end of 2026
Janumet and Janumet XR government-set Medicare prices take effect January 1, 2027; Januvia/Janumet US exclusivity ended May 2026 and Janumet XR ends July 2026

Keytruda: European data exclusivity ends July 2026; US biosimilar competition could begin December 2028; Lenvima IRA price effective January 1, 2028; Keytruda expected IRA price effective January 1, 2029
